correctness.rationale: For n>=3,d|n,m=n/d, every fixed barycentric vector has orbitwise-constant weights, with support a union of H_d orbits; thus geometric fixed spaces are the orbit-union simplicial complex, not an abstract fixed-vertex subcomplex. For odd d=2s+1 the exact maximum original cyclic distance over each pair O_a,O_b equals s*m+delta_m(a,b), including a=b. Hence the entire filtration is empty below sm and otherwise literally VR(C_m;r-sm), with inclusion-natural PL identification; for even d every complete orbit contains antipodes, so only the full simplex stage r>=n/2 has fixed points. The m=1,2 and identity d=1 boundary cases follow from literal quotient metric. The proof is unrestricted in n,d, real r; bounded enumeration is corroboration only.
risks: Geometric realization is essential: abstract vertex-fixed subcomplex can be empty; no homotopy fixed-point or orbit-space quotient conclusion.
No claim about reflection subgroups or irregular polygon metrics.
